title: Supplier portal access through the network
requirement: Supplier users log in once to the Supplier Network (password, MFA; SSO later), see a customer switcher and a unified inbox, and open each customer's screens served with that customer's name, branding context, organisation and rules; inside a customer they see only their supplier's records (SPX-006) and only modules the customer enabled for suppliers.
acceptance_criteria: Given a supplier user connected to two customers, When logged in, Then the inbox shows both customers' items and the switcher lists both.|Given an enterprise user, When they open the network portal, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given customer A disables supplier invoicing, When the supplier works in A, Then invoices are hidden for A only.

title: Portal home
requirement: A home page with counts of orders awaiting acknowledgement, notices due, invoices by status, held or disputed invoices, documents expiring, open tasks and announcements.
acceptance_criteria: Given data, When loaded, Then counts are correct and link to lists.|Given no data, When loaded, Then zeros are shown. (edge)|Given an announcement for suppliers, When published, Then it appears.|Given a supplier user whose supplier is inactive, When the home page loads, Then a status notice is shown and actions are disabled. (error case)

title: Tasks and queries in the portal
requirement: Suppliers see tasks assigned to them (kernel tasks), respond, attach files and resolve; buyers reopen or close.
acceptance_criteria: Given a task assigned, When the supplier resolves it, Then the buyer is notified.|Given a closed task, When the supplier tries to respond, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a task with an attachment, When opened, Then the file is downloadable.
notes: Was FF-158. The tasks are the kernel's (TF-097) when they exist.

title: Supplier portal across organisations
requirement: A supplier user shall see documents, tasks and questionnaires from every organisation of the tenant that enabled the supplier, grouped or filterable by organisation, with the organisation's name, terms and contacts shown on each document; data of organisations that did not enable the supplier is never shown.
rationale: One portal for the supplier, clear separation for the buyer group.
acceptance_criteria: Given enablement in A and B, When the supplier opens orders, Then orders of A and B appear with the organisation shown.|Given no enablement in C, When the supplier opens a C document by identifier, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given an invoice created by the supplier, When saved, Then its organisation equals the order's organisation and the organisation's bill-to details apply.

title: Supplier portal users
requirement: A supplier contact with portal access is a Supplier Network user of the supplier organisation, created by the primary contact in the network; buyers may block a network user for their tenant only.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new network user added by the primary contact, When saved, Then the user can act for every customer per role and appears as a contact in each connected tenant.|Given an email already used in the network, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a tenant blocks a network user, When that user opens the tenant's items, Then they are refused for that tenant only and other customers are unaffected.
notes: Was FF-027, the portal users; the contact data is BF-103.

title: Supplier portal ownership
requirement: Every supplier-facing operation shall arrive from the Supplier Network with a delegated token bound to one supplier relationship and shall be bound to that supplier by a kernel record policy; lists filter to the supplier; access by identifier to another supplier's record is refused and audited with the supplier user identity.
rationale: Gap: missing ownership checks in the current product.
acceptance_criteria: Given supplier A's user requests supplier B's order, When evaluated, Then it is refused and audited. (error case)|Given a list of invoices, When loaded by a supplier user, Then only their invoices appear with correct paging.|Given a buyer impersonating a supplier user, When acting, Then the supplier scope applies and the audit shows both identities.
notes: Was FF-036. Moved from Supplier management (SUP-081 in the checkpoint's skeleton, an identifier not reused) by the design session's answer: a rule every product's supplier views obey (section 4); they cite it and depend on the kernel's TF-035 and TF-234 (ADR-0042).

title: Channels a new supplier starts with
requirement: Tenant administrators shall set the channels a new supplier's documents may reach it by (email, the supplier portal, internal only), written into the new supplier's purchasing profile (PUR-021) and editable per supplier there.
rationale: Consistency and speed; the portal is where a supplier's channels are offered.
acceptance_criteria: Given the default channels email and portal, When a supplier is created, Then its purchasing profile has both.|Given a default changed, When existing suppliers are viewed, Then their channels are unchanged.|Given a user without the portal's configuration permission, When saving the defaults, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-035, BF-106, FF-171 and SUP-005: the portal channels a new supplier starts with, which BF-106 set as a default and SUP-005 as an onboarding setting; one requirement at the review of L2, 2026-10-20 (ADR-0043).

title: Answering without a portal account
requirement: A supplier contact without a Supplier Network account shall answer one information request (SUP-225) through a one-time verified link (TF-246): sent to a contact the customer knows, opened with a code sent to that contact's email address, limited to that one request, and expiring. The page shows the customer's name and nothing else of the customer. A change to a critical field made this way is still verified out of band before it applies (SUP-205). Once the Supplier Network exists, a contact who answered this way is invited to join it.
rationale: Gap G13: some suppliers answer one questionnaire a year and will never use a portal; they should not have to register to do it, and nothing they send this way may skip the customer's checks.
acceptance_criteria: Given a link for an information request, When the contact enters the emailed code, Then only that request's form opens, with the customer's name.|Given a bank account submitted through a link, When the response is approved, Then the account is still verified, automatically or by call-back, before it applies.|Given a link already used to submit, When the contact opens it again, Then it is refused, saying the customer can send a new link. (error case)|Given the Supplier Network in service, When a contact submits through a link, Then the contact is invited to join it.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G13 of the supplier management pack). It works before the Supplier Network exists (S8), so supplier information collection ships with Supplier management (PR1) and moves into the portal with the supplier side (PR8, SPX-029). Accepting one invitation through a link, as TF-246 allows, comes with the invitation itself (SUP-001, PR8). With SUP-225 and SPX-029 it replaces SUP-102, retired.

title: Supplier connection and onboarding through the network
requirement: A customer's invitation shall create a connection request in the Supplier Network; a new supplier registers once (network profile and credentials) and an existing supplier accepts the request; the connection becomes a relationship linked to the customer's supplier record; the customer-specific onboarding wizard (SUP-002) then runs with the network profile pre-filled.
rationale: Decision F-16: one registration for all customers.
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing network supplier invited by a second customer, When they accept, Then no new registration is needed and the second customer's wizard opens with the profile pre-filled.|Given a new supplier, When they complete network registration, Then the first customer's wizard opens next.|Given an invitation to a tax identifier that belongs to a different registered organisation, When sent, Then the network flags the conflict to the buyer before the invitation goes out. (error case)

title: Unified inbox across customers
requirement: The supplier portal shall show one inbox of items needing action across all customers (orders awaiting acknowledgement, shipment notices due, receipts to review, invoices held or disputed, information requests, tasks, documents expiring) with the customer name and organisation on each item, filters by customer, type, status and due date, sorting by due date, and a count per customer.
rationale: Suppliers work for many customers; one list saves time.
acceptance_criteria: Given items from three customers, When the inbox loads, Then all appear with customer and organisation names and due dates.|Given a filter by customer B, When applied, Then only B's items appear.|Given an item whose customer unit is unreachable, When the inbox loads, Then it is marked unreachable and can be retried. (error case)
notes: Was FF-191. Changed 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps): the inbox lists information requests, which replaced questionnaires (SUP-221 to SUP-231, SPX-029).

title: Customer switcher and customer context
requirement: A customer switcher shall set the active customer for all screens (orders, notices, receipts, invoices, catalogue, questionnaires, tasks, company data per customer); screens show the customer's name, organisation, terms and rules; actions run in the customer's tenant with the customer's validations.
rationale: Clear context prevents mistakes across customers.
acceptance_criteria: Given the switcher set to customer A, When orders are listed, Then only A's orders appear with A's branding context.|Given an invoice created under customer A, When submitted, Then A's matching rules and tolerances apply.|Given a user without a relationship to customer C, When they try to switch to C, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Acting on documents of several customers
requirement: Supplier users shall acknowledge orders, submit shipment notices and invoices, answer questionnaires and resolve tasks for any connected customer from the portal; bulk acknowledgement across customers shall run each item in its customer's tenant and report per item.
acceptance_criteria: Given orders from two customers selected, When bulk acknowledged, Then each is acknowledged in its tenant and the results list shows both.|Given one customer rejects an acknowledgement (order cancelled meanwhile), When the bulk action runs, Then the others succeed and the failure shows the customer's reason. (error case)|Given an invoice submitted for customer A, When saved, Then it exists only in A's tenant and the inbox item closes.

title: One profile, per-customer acceptance
requirement: The supplier shall maintain one network profile; each change shall be offered to every connected customer; the supplier shall see per customer whether a change is pending, accepted or declined with the customer's reason; customer-specific data (terms, status, preferred flag, questionnaires, customer-required documents) stays per customer.
rationale: Less duplicate maintenance for suppliers, full control for customers.
acceptance_criteria: Given an address change, When saved, Then each customer shows pending until its approval completes.|Given customer B declines with a reason, When viewed, Then the reason is shown for B only.|Given a change rejected by a customer's validation (for example an unsupported bank code format), When received, Then the supplier sees the validation message for that customer. (error case)
notes: Was FF-194. Since 2026-10-21 a profile change becomes a change request in each customer (SUP-201), and a bank change a critical one (SUP-205); SUP-022 and SUP-023, on which it depended, are retired into them, and the outcome of each field is SPX-030's.

title: Supplier users and roles in the network
requirement: The supplier's primary contact shall manage the supplier organisation's users (invite, roles, remove) in the network; roles decide which customers and which document types a user may work (all customers by default, or a customer subset); customers may block a user for their tenant only.
rationale: Supplier organisations need their own user administration.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user limited to customers A and C, When they log in, Then B's items are not shown.|Given a user removed by the primary contact, When they try to log in, Then it is refused and sessions end. (error case)|Given customer B blocks a user, When that user opens B's items, Then they are refused for B only.

title: Supplier notifications across customers
requirement: Supplier users shall receive notifications from all customers through the network with the customer named, choose channels and digests once for all customers, and never receive a customer's internal notifications; customers keep their templates and branding in the content.
acceptance_criteria: Given orders issued by customers A and B, When the daily digest is chosen, Then one email lists both grouped by customer.|Given a customer's internal notification key, When evaluated, Then it is never routed to supplier users. (error case)|Given an immediate channel chosen for holds, When a hold occurs, Then the notification is sent at once with the customer named.

title: Relationship status and history
requirement: Suppliers shall see each customer relationship with status (connected, on hold, ended), the customer's enabled organisations, terms and performance indicators the customer chooses to share; ended relationships keep read-only history of documents for the retention period.
acceptance_criteria: Given a relationship on hold, When viewed, Then the status and the customer's message are shown and actions are disabled.|Given a customer sharing on-time delivery, When viewed, Then the indicator is shown for that customer only.|Given an ended relationship, When the supplier opens a document, Then it is read-only and no action is offered. (error case)

title: Information requests in the portal
requirement: The supplier shall see every customer's information requests in its inbox (SPX-022), each with the customer, the due date and the state; open one in that customer's context; fill it in with drafts saved and what is still missing shown; confirm or change the pre-filled values; attach evidence with its issue and expiry dates; see a returned section with the reviewer's comment beside each question and edit only that section; and, once submitted, read it with its state.
rationale: Suppliers answer for many customers; one place for every customer's requests, each in its customer's context, is the network's promise.
acceptance_criteria: Given requests from two customers, When the inbox loads, Then each shows its customer, its due date and its state.|Given a returned section, When it is opened, Then the comments show beside their questions and only that section can be edited.|Given an attachment saved with an expiry date in the past, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a submitted response, When viewed, Then it is read-only, with its state.
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the supplier management pack's section 8.3). With SUP-225 and SPX-008 it replaces SUP-102, retired, whose AC2 and AC4 it keeps (AC4 and AC3 here). It obeys the ownership rule (SPX-006).

title: The supplier's change requests and their outcome
requirement: For each customer, the supplier shall see its change requests, whatever their source (its own edits, its network profile, its information responses), with each field's outcome: applied, with its date; waiting, for approval, verification or its effective date; rejected, with the customer's reason; or a question to answer, which it answers there.
rationale: A supplier that does not know whether its new bank account was accepted calls the buyer, or worse, keeps invoicing to the old one.
acceptance_criteria: Given a change request whose address applied and whose phone was rejected, When viewed, Then both outcomes show, the date for one and the reason for the other.|Given a question from the customer's reviewer, When the supplier answers, Then the field returns to the reviewer.|Given another supplier's change request, When asked for by its identifier, Then it is refused (SPX-006). (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, the supplier management pack's section 8.2, rule 1: the supplier sees which changes were applied and why the others were not).
